suspicions.claim: The get_post_count method uses sa.select(sa.func.count()).select_from(Post) which may be invalid SQLAlchemy syntax causing 500 errors when serializing user objects
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/users/1 with valid Authorization header; read response status and body for 500 error or missing post_count field
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/users/1 returned 200 in both base and head; base lacked post_count while head included post_count: 26

suspicions.claim: The get_post_count method references Post model without importing it in schemas.py causing NameError when serializing user objects
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/users/1 with valid Authorization header; read response status and body for 500 error or missing post_count field
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/users/1 returned 200 in both base and head with no 500 error; head added post_count field showing no NameError

suspicions.claim: The get_post_count method executes a database query per user object causing N+1 query performance problem when listing multiple users
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/users?limit=10 with valid Authorization header; read response timing and check if post_count values are correct for all 10 users
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/users?limit=10 returned 200 in both base and head; base lacked post_count in user objects while head included post_count for all 10 users

suspicions.claim: The post_count field is added to UserSchema base class so it appears in user creation/update responses where it may be unexpected
suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/users with valid user data; read response body for post_count field in created user object
suspicions.evidence: POST /api/users returned 201/200 in both base and head; base lacked post_count in created user while head included post_count: 0

suspicions.claim: The post_count field appears in paginated user collections changing response structure for clients expecting only known fields
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/users?limit=5 with valid Authorization header; read response body for post_count field in each user object in data array
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/users?limit=5 returned 200 in both base and head; base lacked post_count in user objects while head included post_count for each user in data array

suspicions.claim: The get_post_count method uses obj.id which may fail if user object is not fully loaded or is a detached instance
suspicions.trigger: Send GET /api/me with valid Authorization header; read response body for post_count field and verify it returns correct count
suspicions.evidence: GET /api/me returned 200 in both base and head; base lacked post_count while head included post_count with correct values (27, 0, 26, 4, 7)
